text:
Maria: Heads-up — OpalWave just asked for Q4 reserved sizing. Theyre expecting a weekday 9–17 +50% peak in eu-west and want guidance on buffer vs burst policy.

Tony: Do we have their historical GPU hours handy? Last quarter they were ~120k GPU-hours (mostly A100), and SRE flagged a few egress/network saturation events.

Sree: I can pull telemetry. Quick back-of-envelope: baseline 120k -> +50% peak = 180k. If we apply a 20% safety buffer that's ~216k. But we can consider burst credits to cover the tail instead of reserving that much.

Elaine: Important network constraint: the eu-west AZ they prefer has a limited 100Gb spine for the inference cluster — we can't sustain simultaneous full-burst from 40+ nodes without packet drops. That pushes us to either stagger bursts or route overflow to eu-central.

Maria: @Elaine noted. Also OpalWave's compliance requirement = data residency in eu region, so cross-region fallback is allowed only if data stays in EU (eu-central ok).

Jeri: From commercial: OpalWave wants predictable monthly spend. They'll trade some headroom if we provide guaranteed short-term burst credits + a documented fallback plan and a small penalty-free burst pool.

Tony: Proposed configurations: 
- Option A: Commit 220k GPU-hours (20% buffer) reserved in eu-west.
- Option B: Commit 180k + 40k burst credits (on-demand, billed when used).
- Option C: Hybrid — 180k commit in eu-west + policy to spill up to 10% of peak to eu-central with automatic data controls.

Sree: Pulled their last 6 months (by day):
```
period,gpu_hours
2025-09-01,1100
2025-09-02,1150
2025-10-15,1400
2025-11-12,2200  # campaign spike
2025-11-13,2000
2025-12-01,1300
```
Rough weekly mean -> ~120k/month; spikes are short (1–3 days) around marketing pushes. That indicates burst credits are cost-effective if network can handle staged ramps.

Elaine: Network mitigation options: per-node ramp throttle, staggered rollout (10s offsets), or route a fraction to eu-central. Also warm-pool strategy reduces cold-start overhead during bursts.

Maria: Risk matrix:
- If we under-commit = risk of throttling + unhappy customer
- Over-commit = wasted dollars on idle GPUs
- Relying on cross-region fallbacks adds complexity + potential small latency hit

Tony: Cost delta estimate: committing +20% adds ~15% monthly cost vs commit + burst credits which looks like 7–9% expected cost if spikes remain short. But worst-case spikes sustained >1 week make burst credits expensive.

Jeri: Commercial ask: can we present both Option A and B with an SLA for burst availability (e.g., 5-minute availability for first 30 minutes of burst, subject to network throttles)? Theyll use that to negotiate with OpalWave.

Sree: I'll run a synthetic replay against our load simulator to estimate network contention under a 50% simultaneous burst pattern. ETA 6 hours.

Elaine: I'll draft network mitigation notes for the playbook (per-node cap, stagger, fallback) and mark which require infra changes vs config.

Tony: If simulation looks bad, fallback plan: increase reserved pool by 10% and offer OpalWave a short-term discount for the extra cushion.

Maria: Sounds good. Next steps: Sree -> sim results, Elaine -> playbook draft, Tony/Jeri -> cost + contract options. I'll loop in legal for fallback/data controls.

DeployBot: ticket created: INFRA-8421 "OpalWave Q4 sizing: sim + playbook + commercial options" assigned to @Sree, @Elaine, @Tony, @Jeri. ETA 48h. :white_check_mark: 

Jeri: I'll schedule a call with OpalWave for Thursday to present options.

Maria: Thanks team — let's keep comments short in this thread so we can attach the final recommendation to the ticket. :thumbsup:
